about: Which branch of a `{platform, select, …}` block each running system reads, so every resolver agrees: `selectReaderFor` + `pickPlatformBranch` + `t()` (platform-select-cases.test.ts), the old-WebKit boot guard's `pickText` (gen-boot-guard-lib.test.ts), the native-strings generator (gen-native-strings.test.ts), and Rust's `native_strings::pick` (native_strings.rs). `systems` maps a platform plus its Linux desktop (`convention('linuxDesktop')`, `null` off Linux) to the reader; `blocks` gives what each reader sees. `linux` is any other desktop and reads `other`. Mechanism: `DETAILS.md` § Platform variants.

blocks.name: a plain value reads the same everywhere
a three-OS block: both desktops read other
blocks.value: {platform, select, macos {Show in Finder} windows {Show in File Explorer} other {Show in file manager}}

blocks.name: no windows branch: Windows reads other
both desktop branches: each desktop reads its own, any other desktop and Windows read other
blocks.value: {platform, select, macos {Show in Finder} linuxGnome {Show in Files} linuxKde {Show in Dolphin} other {Show in file manager}}

blocks.name: only a KDE branch: GNOME reads other
blocks.value: {platform, select, macos {Keychain} windows {Credential Manager} linuxKde {KWallet} other {your keyring}}

blocks.name: only a GNOME branch: KDE reads other
